voyages.name: HMS Beagle: selected ship itinerary, 1831–1836
voyages.summary: FitzRoy’s ship itinerary with selected dated ports and survey waypoints. Darwin’s inland journeys are excluded. Large gaps include repeated South American surveying; the line does not reproduce those cruises. Galápagos departure follows the ship on 20 October, not Darwin’s final shore visit on 17 October.

stops.name: Plymouth, departure
stops.note: Volume II, p. 42. Departure endpoint; no earlier stay is implied.

stops.name: Porto Praia, Santiago
stops.note: Volume II, pp. 51–56. Regional port stay; small sounding movements are not represented.

stops.name: Salvador, Bahia
stops.note: Volume II, pp. 60–63. Port visit; local sounding trips took place during this interval.

stops.name: Rio de Janeiro, second visit
stops.note: Volume II, pp. 77–82. Beagle returned after a separate Bahia cruise. Darwin had remained around Rio; his movements are not used as the ship track.

stops.name: Good Success Bay, Tierra del Fuego
stops.note: Volume II, pp. 119–120. Arrival observation only; later departure is not specified here.

stops.name: Port Famine, Strait of Magellan
stops.note: Volume II, pp. 358–359. Both vessels were moored here by 3 June and sailed on 9 June. The intervening 1833–1834 cruises are omitted; this is not a continuous passage from Tierra del Fuego.

stops.name: Valparaíso
stops.note: Volume II, pp. 361–362. FitzRoy explicitly gives the ship arrival as 22 July. Regional port interval while charts were prepared and Adventure sold.

stops.name: Callao
stops.note: Itinerary, 19 July–7 September 1835; FitzRoy volume II, p. 482. Ship visit corroborated by FitzRoy’s 19 July arrival date. FitzRoy himself rejoined from Blonde on 9 August. Darwin’s separate inland trips are not plotted.

stops.name: San Cristóbal / Chatham Island
stops.note: Volume II, pp. 485–487. Approximate southwestern anchorage; survey then moved to another bay.

stops.name: Tagus Cove, Isabela
stops.note: Volume II, pp. 494–495. Anchoring observation only; the surrounding island surveys are not traced.

stops.name: Darwin / Culpepper Islet, offshore
stops.note: Volume II, p. 501. Offshore departure waypoint, not a landing. Beagle left the archipelago after passing Wenman and Culpepper.

stops.name: Tahiti, Matavai arrival
stops.note: Volume II, pp. 508–510. Arrival observation; later Tahiti anchorages are omitted. FitzRoy changed the calendar from 16 to 17 November during the visit.

stops.name: Bay of Islands
stops.note: Volume II, pp. 563–564 and 610. Regional bay visit; not a claim of remaining at one precise berth.

stops.name: Sydney Cove
stops.note: Volume II, pp. 621–623.

stops.name: Hobart
stops.note: Volume II, pp. 623–624.

stops.name: King George Sound, Albany
stops.note: Volume II, pp. 625–628.

stops.name: Keeling / Cocos Islands
stops.note: Volume II, pp. 628–637. Regional island anchorage; shore work and boats are not separate ship positions.

stops.name: Port Louis, Mauritius
stops.note: Volume II, p. 638.

stops.name: Simon’s Bay
stops.note: Volume II, p. 638. Arrival observation only. Later Atlantic calls listed by FitzRoy are omitted from this sparse selection.

stops.name: Falmouth, arrival
stops.note: Volume II, p. 638. End of selected circumnavigation; ship continued to Greenwich and Woolwich.

voyages.name: Magellan–Elcano expedition: selected anchors, 1519–1522
voyages.summary: Selected fleet and surviving Victoria positions. Magellan died at Mactan on 27 April 1521; subsequent legs belong to the surviving expedition, ultimately under Juan Sebastián Elcano. Strait passages and ocean legs are schematic and do not stand for all five ships after their separation.

stops.name: Sanlúcar de Barrameda, departure
stops.note: Chronological summary; departure from Sanlúcar.

stops.name: Tenerife
stops.note: Chronological summary, September–October 1519.

stops.name: Rio de Janeiro bay
stops.note: Chronological summary, December 1519.

stops.name: Puerto San Julián
stops.note: Chronological summary, wintering at San Julián.

stops.name: Cape Vírgenes, strait approach
stops.note: Chronological summary; strait entered 21 October. Regional observation; no straight strait alignment is asserted.

stops.name: Pacific exit of Strait of Magellan
stops.note: Pigafetta account, entry into Pacific on 28 November.

stops.name: Guam, regional landfall
stops.note: Pigafetta account, 6 March 1521. Island-scale location; exact landing beach is not asserted.

stops.name: Mactan: Magellan’s death
stops.note: Pigafetta account of Mactan, 27 April. Magellan died here. The next leg represents survivors, not his continued travel.

stops.name: Tidore: surviving ships
stops.note: Chronological summary, Tidore arrival and Victoria departure. Victoria continued west; Trinidad did not complete this return route.

stops.name: Cape of Good Hope: Victoria offshore
stops.note: Somos Afro, Victoria return chronology. Offshore passage anchor; no port visit or precise track is implied.

stops.name: Sanlúcar: Victoria returns
stops.note: Pigafetta conclusion and chronological summary. Elcano and survivors returned; this is not Magellan’s personal itinerary.

voyages.name: Lewis and Clark: outward river and land journey, 1804–1806
voyages.summary: Selected outward Corps of Discovery route and the winter at Fort Clatsop. River travel alternates with an overland crossing supported by Shoshone and Nez Perce knowledge, food and horses. Great Falls portage and smaller portages are not resolved. The split return routes of 1806 are deliberately not combined into a fictitious single itinerary.

stops.name: Camp Dubois, departure
stops.note: Clark journal, 14 May 1804. Approximate historical Mississippi–Missouri confluence camp; channels have changed.

stops.name: Fort Mandan
stops.note: Journals, 2 November 1804 and 7 April 1805. Winter camp construction began in early November; regional location, not the modern replica.

stops.name: Camp Fortunate
stops.note: Journals, 17 and 24 August 1805. Canoe-to-horse transition in the Beaverhead headwaters, now inundated by Clark Canyon Reservoir; Sacagawea and Shoshone assistance were central.

stops.name: Travelers’ Rest, outward
stops.note: Journals, 9–11 September 1805. Overland crossing; straight links are not Lolo Trail geometry.

stops.name: Canoe Camp, Clearwater
stops.note: Journals, 26 September and 7 October 1805. Nez Perce assistance enabled construction of the canoes; departure on 7 October.

stops.name: Fort Clatsop
stops.note: House Report 107-456, historical background. Winter camp interval. This selected outward itinerary ends at departure; the 1806 return is recorded separately.

voyages.name: Columbus: selected first-voyage anchors, 1492–1493
voyages.summary: Selected anchors from the surviving Las Casas abstract. The Bahamas landfall and some Caribbean locations remain debated; broad regional anchors are used. Indigenous peoples already inhabited these places. The expedition involved coercion and captivity, and later return legs do not represent Santa María, which was wrecked.

stops.name: Palos, departure
stops.note: Journal, 3 August 1492.

stops.name: La Gomera, departure
stops.note: Journal, 6 September 1492. Departure observation; the preceding island movements are not resolved.

stops.name: Guanahaní, Bahamas: uncertain island
stops.note: Journal, night of 11–12 October 1492. Archipelago-scale anchor only. This coordinate does not identify the disputed landfall island or prove a specific beach.

stops.name: Northeastern Cuba, regional arrival
stops.note: Journal, 28 October 1492. Regional coast anchor; modern identification of the harbor is not asserted.

stops.name: Northern Hispaniola: Santa María wreck
stops.note: Journal, 25 December 1492. Approximate coastal region. Later travel is the surviving expedition, not the wrecked Santa María.

stops.name: Lisbon
stops.note: Journal, 4–13 March 1493. Regional Tagus anchorage; weather and movement within the estuary are not resolved.

stops.name: Palos, return
stops.note: Journal, 15 March 1493.

voyages.name: Cabrillo–Ferrelo: selected documented ports, 1542–1543
voyages.summary: A sparse set of dated ports and regional anchors. The northern coastal cruises beyond the Channel Islands are not reconstructed. Cabrillo died on 3 January 1543; Bartolomé Ferrelo led the later voyage. The Channel Islands coordinate is regional: neither a precise burial island nor an uncertain far-northern landfall is asserted.

stops.name: Navidad, departure
stops.note: Juan Rodríguez Cabrillo, voyage account.

stops.name: San Diego Bay
stops.note: 1959 brochure, voyage chronology. Kumeyaay homeland; bay-scale anchor, not a claim of first human arrival.

stops.name: Western Channel Islands, regional anchor
stops.note: 1959 brochure, Further Exploration and Cabrillo’s Death. Arrival at the island called Posesión in the account. Modern island identification is uncertain; the coordinate represents a region, not a fixed burial or anchorage site.

stops.name: Western Channel Islands: Cabrillo’s death
stops.note: Juan Rodríguez Cabrillo, death on 3 January 1543. Regional death location only; exact island disputed. Ferrelo led the surviving expedition thereafter.

stops.name: Cedros Island: ships reunited
stops.note: 1959 brochure, Northernmost Limit and Return. Dated reunion of the ships. Intervening northern cruising and separation are omitted.

stops.name: Navidad: Ferrelo’s return
stops.note: 1959 brochure, voyage conclusion. Return endpoint under Ferrelo, not continued travel by Cabrillo.

voyages.name: Cook and Endeavour: selected outward stops, 1768–1770
voyages.summary: Selected outward portion of the first Endeavour voyage, ending at departure from the Endeavour River. The later Batavia and homeward voyage are not animated. Tupaia’s navigation and interpretation and existing Pacific communities are essential context. Dates retain Cook’s manuscript convention.

stops.name: Plymouth, departure
stops.note: Endeavour journal introduction, 26 August 1768.

stops.name: Rio de Janeiro
stops.note: Daily entries, 13 November and 5 December 1768. Departure from anchorage; clearing the bay took longer.

stops.name: Good Success Bay
stops.note: Daily entries, 15–21 January 1769.

stops.name: Matavai Bay, Tahiti
stops.note: Daily entries, 13 April and 13 July 1769. Regional visit including the Venus observation; this is not an empty island or a claim of uninterrupted ship immobility.

stops.name: Ship Cove / Meretoto
stops.note: Daily entries, 16 January and 7 February 1770. Selected New Zealand anchorage; the earlier circumnavigation and coastal stops are omitted.

stops.name: Botany Bay
stops.note: Daily entries, 29 April and 6 May 1770. The landing met armed resistance; the encounter occurred in already inhabited country.

stops.name: Endeavour River / Waalumbaal
stops.note: Daily entries, 17 June and 4 August 1770. Repair anchorage after reef damage; departure is explicit in the 4 August entry.

voyages.name: Tasman: documented New Zealand coastal phase, 1642–1643
voyages.summary: A short documented phase of the Heemskerck and Zeehaen voyage. It does not reconstruct the Mauritius, Tasmania, Tonga, Fiji or return legs. Tasman’s crews observed inhabited Māori coasts; the dated anchors are ship observations, not landings.

stops.name: West coast of South Island, offshore
stops.note: Te Ara chronology, 13 December 1642. Latitude is reported; longitude is a broad modern anchor south of Cape Foulwind.

stops.name: Mohua / Golden Bay
stops.note: First contact between Māori and Europeans, 18–19 December 1642. Encounter with Ngāti Tūmatakōkiri; four Dutch crew were killed on 19 December. Exact anchorage is not asserted.

stops.name: Three Kings / Manawatāwhi offshore
stops.note: Te Ara chronology, 4–6 January 1643. Boats attempted to obtain water; ships anchored nearby and left New Zealand on 6 January. No landing is asserted.

voyages.name: Drake: selected outward anchors to California, 1577–1579
voyages.summary: Selected anchors from the outward part of the circumnavigation. This sparse series omits Atlantic provisioning, South American raids, and most Pacific stops. The California harbor remains debated; the Point Reyes regional anchor is not an exact landing claim. The return to Plymouth in 1580 is not animated.

stops.name: Plymouth, departure
stops.note: The famous voyage, opening chronology.

stops.name: Strait of Magellan, eastern entrance
stops.note: World Encompassed, entry into strait on 20 August 1578. Observed passage waypoint, not a stop interval.

stops.name: Strait of Magellan, Pacific exit
stops.note: World Encompassed, exit on 6 September 1578. Storms and southern detours after the exit are not reconstructed.

stops.name: Point Reyes region, debated harbor
stops.note: Francis Drake, California landfall narrative. Arrival date only. NPS describes competing harbor locations; this point represents the region, not an adjudicated exact site.

voyages.name: Vancouver: selected coastal observations in 1792
voyages.summary: Three documented observations or encounters within the 1791–1795 expedition. This is not the full survey track; boat excursions, ship movements and long gaps cannot be reconstructed as continuous travel from these anchors alone.

stops.name: Puget Sound, Point Lawton vicinity
stops.note: USGS account, Vancouver sighting of Mount St. Helens on 19 May 1792. Regional survey observation, not a precise Discovery anchorage.

stops.name: Yuquot / Nootka Sound
stops.note: BC Studies account of Vancouver and Maquinna, 28 August 1792. Documented encounter anchor in Mowachaht territory; duration is not inferred.

stops.name: Off Columbia River mouth
stops.note: USGS account, naming Mount St. Helens on 20 October 1792. Offshore observation only; Broughton’s later river survey is a different journey.

voyages.name: Bering and St. Peter: documented outbound anchors, 1741
voyages.summary: Two secure dated anchors for the outbound voyage to Alaska. St. Peter is Bering’s ship; Chirikov’s St. Paul followed a separate route. The subsequent Aleutian voyage, wreck on Bering Island and crew return are not reconstructed here. Dates retain the account’s Old Style convention.

stops.note: Smithsonian Contributions to Anthropology 7, p. 108. Departure endpoint; not a claim that the Pacific crossing was a straight line.

stops.name: Kayak Island, western shore
stops.note: Smithsonian Contributions to Anthropology 7, p. 108. Anchorage and Steller’s landing date; approximate island-shore location. No return leg is inferred.
